After Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo today, the company rolled out a suite of new resources to help developers prepare their apps for its first foldable iPhone. Here's what you need to know.

Apple Shares iPhone Duo Resources with Developers

Apple announced the iPhone Duo this morning at its "Surprise and Shine" event. The device, the company's first foldable phone, was unveiled alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 with active noise cancellation.

In addition to revealing iPhone Duo details to the general public and sharing device-related assets on its Design Resources platform, Apple has also added a dedicated page offering several resources to help developers get their apps ready for the new foldable device.

These include two iPhone Duo Group Labs sessions scheduled for September 16 and 17, as well as Q&A sessions on Photos and Camera, SwiftUI, and UIKit, with two time slots each on September 23.

Apple will also host iPhone Duo Workshops in locations around the world, offering hands-on sessions for developers to optimise their apps and "explore adaptability across all screen sizes." These workshops will begin later this month.

The "Get ready for iPhone Duo" page also lists several upcoming tools and documentation, including Xcode 27.1 beta, "Designing for iPhone Duo," and "Preparing your app for iPhone Duo."

The page also features the following six WWDC-style session videos:

  • Design for iPhone Duo
  • Prepare your app for iPhone Duo
  • Raise the bar with iPhone Duo
  • Strike a pose with adaptive layouts on iPhone Duo
  • Leverage multiple displays and scenes on iPhone Duo
  • Build a great camera experience for iPhone Duo

You can check out the full range of developer resources Apple has made available for iPhone Duo here.
